title: compiler-sfc: recursive type + indexed access makes compileScript walk a cyclic AST (RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded)
body:
Vue version
3.6.0-rc.2

Link to minimal reproduction
https://play.vuejs.org/#
Steps to reproduce
The repro has four files. App.vue reads a recursive type through an indexed access type
(TreeNode['parent']), and Second.vue / Third.vue are identical components whose props
type resolves to that same recursive type.
After opening the link, click two tabs in the file bar:

Click the Second.vue tab. It compiles fine.
Click the Third.vue tab. compileScript throws.

The clicks are only needed because the Playground compiles files lazily, one per active tab.
What matters is the sequence of three compileScript calls in a single process:

the component using TreeNode['parent'] (the indexed access)
a component whose props type resolves to TreeNode
a second component whose props type resolves to TreeNode — this one throws

The files:
// types.ts
export type TreeNode = {
  parent?: TreeNode;
};

export type ItemProps = {
  node?: TreeNode;
};
<!-- App.vue -->
<script setup lang="ts">
import { type TreeNode } from './types.ts';
import Second from './Second.vue';
import Third from './Third.vue';

defineProps<{ parentNode?: TreeNode['parent'] }>();
</script>

<template>
  <Second />
  <Third />
</template>
<!-- Second.vue and Third.vue, identical -->
<script setup lang="ts">
import { type ItemProps } from './types.ts';

defineProps<ItemProps>();
</script>

<template>
  <div />
</template>
Reproduces the same way outside the Playground, in plain Node against
@vue/compiler-sfc@3.6.0-rc.2, by calling compileScript on the three files in that order.
It also reproduces with the esm-browser build, with and without registerTS, and with both
a real filesystem and an in-memory fs option.
What is expected?
All three components compile, as they do on 3.5.40.
Same files, same click sequence, Vue 3.5.40 (control):
https://play.vuejs.org/#
What is actually happening?
compileScript throws:
RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded
    at SyncWalker.visit (@vue/compiler-sfc@3.6.0-rc.2/dist/compiler-sfc.esm-browser.js)
    at SyncWalker.visit (…)
    at SyncWalker.visit (…)
    … ~5400 frames

Cause. resolveTypeReference caches the resolved declaration on the reference node itself:
return canCache ? (node._resolvedReference = resolved) : resolved
_resolvedReference holds an AST node, so it has a .type string. compileScript then walks
each top-level <script setup> statement with estree-walker, whose visit iterates every
enumerable own key and recurses into any value with a .type string. It therefore follows
_resolvedReference as if it were an AST child. Once a recursive type has had its recursive
member resolved, the reference graph contains a back-edge, and the walk never terminates.
Instrumenting the walker on the real-world case gives the closed loop (the last node is already
an ancestor):
(root):VariableDeclaration
  -> declarations[0]:VariableDeclarator "props"
  -> init:CallExpression                          // defineProps<Props>()
  -> typeParameters:TSTypeParameterInstantiation
  -> params[0]:TSTypeReference "Props"
  -> _resolvedReference:TSIntersectionType
  -> types[0]:TSTypeReference "Omit"
  -> typeParameters:TSTypeParameterInstantiation
  -> params[0]:TSTypeReference "BudgetCreateStepsControlsProps"
  -> _resolvedReference:TSTypeLiteral {11 members}
  -> members[1]:TSPropertySignature "budget"
  -> typeAnnotation:TSTypeAnnotation
  -> typeAnnotation:TSTypeReference "Budget"
  -> _resolvedReference:TSTypeLiteral {63 members}
  -> members[45]:TSPropertySignature "parent"     // parent?: Budget & { … }
  -> typeAnnotation:TSTypeAnnotation
  -> typeAnnotation:TSIntersectionType
  -> types[0]:TSTypeReference "Budget"            // back to the ancestor above

The _resolvedReference caching line is identical in 3.5.40 and 3.6.0-rc.2, so the caching is
not itself new. What changed is that on 3.6 the back-edge is reachable from the statement AST
that compileScript walks. On 3.5.40 the same file set produces no reachable back-edge.
Verification. Skipping that single key in the walk clears it. Patching the walker to ignore
_resolvedReference let all 3896 SFCs in our application compile on 3.6.0-rc.2, where the
unpatched compiler crashes. Ignoring every _-prefixed key works too.
A possible fix is to make these internal caches non-enumerable, for example
Object.defineProperty(node, '_resolvedReference', { value: resolved, writable: true, configurable: true, enumerable: false }),
so for…in-based walkers cannot mistake them for AST children. The same applies to any other
internal annotation attached to AST nodes that holds a node.
System Info
  System:
    OS: macOS 26.6
    CPU: (10) arm64 Apple M4
    Memory: 887.94 MB / 16.00 GB
    Shell: 5.9 - /bin/zsh
  Binaries:
    Node: 24.18.0 - /opt/homebrew/opt/node@24/bin/node
    npm: 11.16.0 - /opt/homebrew/opt/node@24/bin/npm
    pnpm: 11.15.1 - /opt/homebrew/opt/node@24/bin/pnpm
  Browsers:
    Chrome: 150.0.7871.187
    Firefox: 153.0.1
    Safari: 26.6
  npmPackages:
    vue: 3.6.0-rc.2 => 3.6.0-rc.2
Any additional comments?
Found while upgrading a Vue 3 application (about 3900 SFCs, Vite 8.1.5,
@vitejs/plugin-vue 6.0.8) from 3.5.40 to 3.6.0-rc.2. The only change was the vue version.
In a real project the failure looks non-deterministic, which made it confusing to diagnose:

The production build failed on one component, the dev server on a different one. Which file
crashes depends on the order in which the shared type-resolution cache gets warmed, not on
anything about the file itself.
Every crashing component compiles fine on its own. It only fails once other components have
been compiled in the same process.
In dev, the resulting Vite error overlay then blocks unrelated interactions, so the visible
symptom appears in features that have nothing to do with the types involved.

title: Custom elements: async components nested ≥3 levels crash with `TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading 'provides')` — chained child resolve races its parent's mount
Suspense: flushing buffered effects overflows the call stack when many effects accumulate while pending (RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded)
body:
Vue version
3.5.39 (also reproduces on 3.5.40 / @b5f8518 in the playground)
Link to minimal reproduction
https://play.vuejs.org/#
Steps to reproduce

Open the playground and show the Preview pane.
The app renders a <Suspense> whose default slot contains an async component (resolves after ~4s) plus a large tree (2000 rows, each with a few flush: 'post' watchers).
While the suspense is pending, a timer keeps mutating a ref, so the still-mounted tree re-renders repeatedly. Each re-render buffers its post effects into suspense.effects (via queueEffectWithSuspense).
When the async component resolves, the suspense flushes the buffered effects.

What is expected?
The buffered effects flush and the app keeps working.
What is actually happening?
Uncaught (in promise): RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded — thrown from queuePostFlushCb called by suspense.resolve():
RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded
    at queuePostFlushCb (runtime-core.esm-bundler.js:331)
    at Object.resolve   (runtime-core.esm-bundler.js:7426)

The scheduler dies mid-flush, leaving the app permanently wedged (blank page).
Root cause
suspense.effects is unbounded — every post effect of every component under a pending suspense boundary is buffered into it. On resolve, the whole array is flushed with a spread call:

scheduler.ts: pendingPostFlushCbs.push(...cb)
scheduler.ts (flushPostFlushCbs nested case): activePostFlushCbs.push(...deduped)
Suspense.ts (merge into pending parent): parent.effects.push(...effects)

Spreading an array into a function call is limited by the engine's call stack (~100k–200k args in V8), so once enough effects accumulate the flush itself throws.
Real-world impact
We hit this in production in a Nuxt app: a kanban board page with ~1000 mounted cards that re-renders once per second (elapsed-time ticker). Navigating to another page keeps the board mounted under <NuxtPage>'s pending Suspense; its buffered effects exceed the spread limit and every SPA navigation away from the board crashes with a permanent white screen (hard reload of the target URL works fine, since there is no pending suspense in that case).
Suggested fix
Replace the unbounded spread pushes with plain loops. I have a PR ready with the fix and a regression test (queuePostFlushCb with a 1M-entry array).

title: compileScript drops template imports from __returned__ when analysis re-runs on a transformed template AST
body:
Vue version
3.5.40
Link to minimal reproduction
https://stackblitz.com/edit/vitejs-vite-evwepvbu?file=package.json
Steps to reproduce
Compile more than 500 unique SFCs for client + SSR (non-inline mode), share each file's descriptor between the two passes (the same way  @vitejs/plugin-vue does). The client pass compileTemplate changes the shared template.ast in place, when the analysis cache (capped at 500) evicts a file entry, its SSR compileScript pass re-runs the import usage analysis on that already transformed AST
What is expected?
__returned__ contains every import the template references, same output as when fewer than 500 templates are compiled. The analysis should re-parse when the AST was already transformed, the same guard compileTemplate has with if (inAST?.transformed) in line 214.
What is actually happening?
Imports referenced only from template expressions or with v-for are dropped from __returned__. While the render function still emits $setup.foo(...) and throws TypeError: $setup.foo is not a function at runtime. Because it only happens with more than 500 unique templates it only comes up in large apps in development, in production builds the template are inlined and are unaffected.
System Info

Any additional comments?
Might be the cause for vitejs/vite-plugin-vue#764, vitest-dev/vitest#9855?

title: SSR memory leak - options API watchers are created and never stopped with async `setup()`
defineModel: named model with PropType + factory default infers wrong generic (regression from #14968)
body:
Vue version
3.5.39
Link to minimal reproduction
https://play.vuejs.org/#
Steps to reproduce
In the reproduction, broken declares a named model with a runtime type: PropType<string[]> plus a factory default: () => []. fixed declares the same thing but with the generic pinned explicitly (defineModel<string[]>(...)).
Run the type checker (or vue-tsc --noEmit locally) over this SFC.
What is expected?
Both broken and fixed should type-check cleanly — this is the recommended pattern for avoiding shared mutable state (per #14966 / #14968): a factory default combined with a runtime PropType declaration.
What is actually happening?
Only broken fails. TS infers the generic T from the default factory function's own type (() => never[]) instead of from the type: PropType<string[]> field:
error TS2769: No overload matches this call.
Overload 1 of 4, '(name: string, options: ({ required: true; } | { default: DefineModelDefault<() => never[]>; }) & Omit<PropOptions<() => never[], () => never[]>, "default"> & DefineModelOptions<...>): ModelRef<...>', gave the following error.
Type 'PropType<string[]>' is not assignable to type 'true | PropType<() => never[]> | null | undefined'.
Type 'new (...args: any[]) => string[]' is not assignable to type 'true | PropType<() => never[]> | null | undefined'.
Type 'new (...args: any[]) => string[]' is not assignable to type 'new (...args: any[]) => () => never[]'.
Type 'string[]' is not assignable to type '() => never[]'.
Type 'string[]' provides no match for the signature '(): never[]'.
Overload 2 of 4, '(name: string, options?: DefineModelRuntimeOptions<string[], string[], string[]> | undefined): ModelRef<string[] | undefined, string, string[] | undefined, string[] | undefined>', gave the following error.
Object literal may only specify known properties, and 'default' does not exist in type 'DefineModelRuntimeOptions<string[], string[], string[]>'.
his is a regression from #14968 (landed in 3.5.39), which introduced DefineModelDefault<T> = InferDefault<Data, T> for the named-model overload. When both a runtime type: PropType<T> field and a factory default are present on the same options object, TS resolves T from the default field first, breaking a pattern that worked prior to 3.5.39.
Workaround: explicitly pin the generic, as shown by fixed in the reproduction:
const fixed = defineModel<string[]>('visibility2', {
  type: Array as PropType<string[]>,
  default: () => [],
})
System Info
vue: 3.5.39
vue-tsc: 3.3.7
typescript: 5.7.3
Any additional comments?
Related to / regression from #14966 and #14968. Only reproduces on the named defineModel(name, options) overload when type/PropType and a factory default are combined; the unnamed defineModel<T>({ ... }) form with an explicit generic is unaffected.

title: hydrateOnVisible: Cannot read properties of null (reading 'nodeType') when the SSR node is detached before the IntersectionObserver callback fires
body:
Vue version
3.5.33
Link to minimal reproduction
https://stackblitz.com/edit/vitejs-vite-ktsycrrc?file=repro.mjs
Steps to reproduce

SSR-render an async component that uses hydrate: hydrateOnVisible().
On the client, hydration is deferred and the strategy registers an IntersectionObserver on the component's SSR node.
The node gets detached from the document before the observer's callback executes (in production this is a route change / re-render while the intersection callback is already queued).
The observer callback runs and invokes hydrate() against the now-detached node.

What is expected?
A node that is no longer connected to the document should simply not be hydrated (there's nothing to hydrate), no exception thrown.
What is actually happening?
hydrate() reaches hydrateNode, which computes the container type from the node's parent:
// packages/runtime-core/src/hydration.ts — inside hydrateNode, async-component branch
nextNode = vnode.type.hydrate(
  node, vnode, parentComponent, parentSuspense,
  getContainerType(parentNode(node)),   // parentNode(node) === null for a detached node
  slotScopeIds, optimized, rendererInternals, hydrateNode,
)

// packages/runtime-core/src/hydration.ts
const getContainerType = (container) => {
  if (container.nodeType !== 1) return undefined   // <-- container is null -> throws
  ...
}

For a detached node parentNode(node) is null, so getContainerType(null) throws TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading 'nodeType').
The async-component hydration wrapper only guards against the patched case, never against disconnection:
// packages/runtime-core/src/apiAsyncComponent.ts — __asyncHydrate
const performHydrate = () => {
  if (patched) { /* warn + */ return }   // only guards `patched`
  hydrate()                              // no isConnected check
}

Because the strategy runs inside load().then(...), the throw surfaces as an unhandledrejection, so app-level try/catch around the component can't catch it.
System Info
vue: 3.5.33
@vue/server-renderer: 3.5.33
Environment where it triggers: Android WebView (Chrome), production SSR + client hydration
Any additional comments?
We see this almost exclusively on Android Chrome WebView (~43k occurrences / ~12.8k users over a rollout window) on a page that lazy-hydrates several below-the-fold sections via hydrateOnVisible. The IntersectionObserver callback is dispatched asynchronously; when the user navigates/re-renders in the WebView, the observed node is detached between the intersection being recorded and the callback running, exactly the sequence above. Desktop rarely hits the race.
Skip hydration when the anchor node is no longer connected. the semantically correct place is the async performHydrate (or each built-in strategy's trigger), e.g. bail when no observed/anchor element isConnected:
const performHydrate = () => {
  if (patched) { return }
  if (el && !el.isConnected) return   // detached before hydration → nothing to hydrate
  hydrate()
}

As defense-in-depth, getContainerType could also tolerate a null container (if (!container || container.nodeType !== 1) return undefined), since it's called with parentNode(node) at several sites.
We're currently shipping a userland wrapper around hydrateOnVisible that applies exactly the isConnected guard, which fully stops the crash.

title: EffectScope stop() causes runtime crash (Cannot read properties of undefined) when dynamic scope cleanup mutates parent.scopes array during traversal
body:
Vue version
3.5.28
Link to minimal reproduction
https://play.vuejs.org/#
Steps to reproduce
Open the reproduction link.
Click the "Trigger сrash" button.
Observe the output status on the screen or check the browser console.
What is expected?
The parent scope should stop all its children successfully. When a child scope stops a sibling scope during the cleanup phase, the parent traversal loop should handle the array mutation gracefully without throwing errors.
What is actually happening?
The application crashes with the following error: TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'stop')
This happens because EffectScope.stop loops over this.scopes using a cached length l. During iteration, one child's onScopeDispose calls stop() on its sibling. The sibling removes itself from the parent's scopes array, reducing the array size. When the parent loop continues to the cached index l, it tries to access an element out of bounds (which is undefined), causing the runtime crash.
System Info
System: OS: macOS, Browser: Chrome, Node: v20.19.5
Any additional comments?
The bug lies in packages/reactivity/src/effectScope.ts.
Inside EffectScope, the methods pause(), resume(), and stop() loop over this.scopes using a cached length without accounting for array mutations. Creating a shallow copy of the array before iterating (e.g. const scopes = this.scopes.slice()) safely resolves the issue.

title: SSR hydration warning: dynamic props on SVG elements are patched as properties instead of attributes
body:
Version
3.5.39
Reproduction link
stackblitz.com
Steps to reproduce

Open the reproduction.
Open the browser devtools Console.
Observe the [Vue warn]: Failed setting prop … error logged during hydration.

What is expected?
During hydration, dynamic props on SVG (and MathML) elements width, height, viewBox, etc.  should be patched as attributes (via setAttribute) exactly as they are during normal client-side rendering. Hydration should be silent.
What is actually happening?
Since 3.5.39, dynamic props on SVG elements are patched as DOM properties during hydration, which throws for read-only SVG IDL properties:
[Vue warn]: Failed setting prop "viewBox" on <svg>: value 0 0 24 24 is invalid.
TypeError: Cannot set property viewBox of #<SVGSVGElement> which has only a getter
    at patchDOMProp
    at patchProp
    at hydrateElement
    at hydrateNode
    at hydrateSubTree
    at <App>

Nothing is visually broken but the console is flooded with warnings.

We ran across this issue in a Nuxt app but I believe the issue is coming from Vue core

title: SSR memory leak after a render error in a dynamic component
body:
Vue version
3.5.39
Link to minimal reproduction
https://stackblitz.com/edit/vitejs-vite-qfkzyzwp?file=leak.mjs
Steps to reproduce

download the reproduction from stackblitz (won't work there, needs to be run locally)
run pnpm i && pnpm leak
see the heap size & alive app instances grow with each request after the single failed render

The script renders 500 fresh SSR apps, which all get garbage-collected. Then renders one app whose slot content throws, then renders 500 more identical healthy apps, which will never be garbage collected afterwards.
A dynamic component <component :is> with a <slot /> is needed for this to reproduce.
Card
<script setup>
    defineProps({ tag: { type: String, default: 'div' } })
</script>

<template>
    <component :is="tag" class="card">
        <slot />
    </component>
</template>
app:
<script setup>
    defineProps(['payload'])  // one request renders with `payload: null` → throws
</script>

<template>
    <main>
        <Card>{{ payload.title }}</Card>
    </main>
</template>
What is expected?
A failed renderToString should not affect subsequent renders and all apps rendered after it should get garbage collected.
What is actually happening?
Every app created after the single failed render is kept in memory forever.
--- phase 1: 500 healthy renders ---
after 500: created=500 finalized=500 alive=0 heap=20.6MB

--- one crashing render (SSR render error) ---
render rejected as expected: Cannot read properties of null (reading 'title')

--- phase 2: 500 healthy renders (identical to phase 1) ---
after 500: created=1001 finalized=500 alive=501 heap=29.0MB

FINAL: created=1001 finalized=500 alive=501

System Info

Any additional comments?
No response

title: Scoped slot transforms array argument if rendered conditionally
body:
Vue version
3.5.0
Link to minimal reproduction
https://play.vuejs.org/#
Steps to reproduce

Create a component with a scoped slot that is rendered conditionally
Pass an array as the sole argument to the slot

What is expected?
Array is rendered normally.
If you render items of that array in v-for loop, you only see items inside that array
What is actually happening?
Array is transformed into object. Items and their indexes are staying the same, key field is added

System Info

Any additional comments?
key attribute is generated by the compiler for the slot rendered with v-if.

While this is not explicitly mentioned in documentation, one can assume that the expectation is that slotProps is always an object, as this is what will be passed to the slot if you use multiple v-bind directives on the slot.
This issue is rather pointing out the difference in behavior of the slot when v-if is present or not present.

title: Function refs on components are invoked before exposed template refs become available since 3.5.39
body:
Vue version
3.5.39
Link to minimal reproduction
https://play.vuejs.org/#
Steps to reproduce
Open the playground with Vue 3.5.39 — it shows "resolved: NO". Switch the version to 3.5.38 — it shows "resolved: YES"
What is expected?
There should be a supported way for component function refs to access exposed template refs, for example through an exposed nativeElement.
Currently, function refs are invoked synchronously during patching, while template ref objects are assigned later in a post-render job. This means that during mount, an exposed template ref is not available yet inside the function ref and will still be null.
What is actually happening?
Before 3.5.39, reading an exposed template ref inside a function ref caused the callback to be re-invoked after the exposed template ref was assigned because the access was tracked by the parent component's render effect.
After #14985 paused tracking during function ref invocation, the callback is invoked only once, before the exposed template ref is assigned, and is never invoked again. Consequently, a function ref no longer has an opportunity to access an exposed template ref.

title: v-model on <select multiple> uses stale collection type after switching between Array and Set
body:

Link to minimal reproduction
https://play.vuejs.org/#__PROD__
Steps to reproduce

Bind a <select multiple v-model> to an Array.
Switch the bound value to a Set at runtime.
Interact with the select again.
The emitted model becomes an Array again.
Switching back from Set -> Array shows the same stale-type behavior in reverse.

What is expected?
The current collection type should be respected after the model switches at runtime.

The change handler keeps using the collection type captured when the directive was created, so the first user interaction after a runtime Array/Set switch emits the old type.

title: Inconsistency in the validation of defaults between `withDefaults` and `defineModel`
compiler-sfc: Reactive Props Destructure rewrites local references to `var` declaration
compiler-core: :key expression not prefixed when element has v-memo without v-for (ReferenceError at runtime)
body:
Version
3.5.35
Reproduction link
play.vuejs.org/
Steps to reproduce
Open the playground link; it throws on load.
The trigger is v-memo + dynamic :key on a plain element without v-for, where the key references a prop
What is expected?
:key expression is prefixed like any other (__props.updateKey / _ctx.updateKey), as in ≤3.5.12
What is actually happening?
transformExpression skips the :key expression whenever the element has v-memo (the !(memo && arg.content === 'key') check added in 99009ee / PR #12014), assuming transformFor processed it eagerly — but that only happens when v-for is also present.
Plain elements fall through → unprefixed key → ReferenceError at runtime

This happened after vue version update.
We hit this in a component library's scroll-container component. It renders custom scrollbars, so its reactive scroll state changes on every scroll frame; to keep large slotted content (e.g. a table body with thousands of cells) from re-rendering on each frame, the content wrapper uses v-memo="[updateKey]" with :key="updateKey" on the same element — "freeze this subtree, and when the parent bumps updateKey (data reload, layout change), rebuild it from scratch instead of diffing."
This compiled and ran correctly up to compiler 3.5.12; from 3.5.13 the generated render function references the key as a bare identifier and every page using the component throws ReferenceError on first render.
Current workaround: v-bind="{ key: updateKey }" instead of :key="updateKey", which bypasses the skipped code path and produces a correctly prefixed expression.

title: watch([], cb, { immediate: true }) // cb not runing as expected
body:
Vue version
3.5.35
Link to minimal reproduction



Steps to reproduce
import { expect, it, vi } from 'vitest'
import { watch } from 'vue' // vue@2.7
import { watch as watch3 } from 'vue3' // "vue3": "npm:vue@^3.5.35"

it('watch([], cb, { immediate: true })', async () => {
  const cb = vi.fn()
  watch([], cb, { immediate: true })
  const cb2 = vi.fn()
  watch3([], cb2, { immediate: true })

  expect(cb2).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1) // but get 0
  expect(cb).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1) // but get 0
})

A: 为什么要 watch 空数组
A: Why watch an empty array?
Q: 封装公共函数时，可以传入不定个数的参数, 比如：
Q: When encapsulating a public function, you can pass a variable number of arguments, for example:
function foo<T extends WatchSource[]>(...args: T) {
  return function wrapper(...args: T) {
     watch(args, cb, { immediate: true })
     ....
  }
}
一般情况下传参，一切正常；但未传参时，cb不执行，不符合语义和直觉
Under normal circumstances with arguments passed, everything works fine; but when no arguments are passed, the callback doesn't execute, which goes against intuition.
What is expected?
expect(cb2).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1)
expect(cb).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1)
What is actually happening?
0

Any additional comments?

title: v-show on enter animation would be different from v-if or v-for in TransitionGroup
body:
Version
3.5.35
Reproduction link
play.vuejs.org/
Steps to reproduce

Turn on the check box next to "toggle visibility of a box" on the top and see how the boxes in Transition will work
Turn on the checkbox 2, 3, or 4 under "Toggle Menu for the following TransitionGroups" and see how the boxes in TransitionGroup will work

Any additional comments?
This is a continuation of the regression chain that started in 3.5.31:

PR #8619 (3.5.31) introduced pendingMounts so teleports defer their mount when parentSuspense.pendingBranch is set. This is what created the situation where a teleport's children can have vnode.component === null.
Issue #14640 + PR #14642 (3.5.32) added the pendingMount check shown above. That gates DOM removal of element children, not the unmountComponent(null, …) call on component children.
Issue #14699 (3.5.32)  reported the same crash with the same stack as this issue. Closed by the author with a note about re-filing with a more accurate reproduction.
Issue #14701 + PR #14702 (3.5.33) added pendingMounts.has(vnode) guard, but only in moveTeleport. The TeleportImpl.remove path was not touched, so 3.5.33 and 3.5.34 still crash.

title: <Transition mode="out-in"> + <Suspense> inside a <template v-if> fragment leaks DOM on toggle
body:
Vue version
3.5.30
Link to minimal reproduction
https://stackblitz.com/edit/vitejs-vite-assboxgb
Steps to reproduce
Hi Vue team,
when toggling between two <template v-if> branches that each contain a <Transition mode="out-in"> wrapping a <Suspense> with an async-setup component, every toggle leaves the previous DOM subtree behind in the container.After N clicks you end up with N+1 copies of the async child rendered. Sibling nodes in the same Fragment (e.g. an <h4>) are removed correctly - only the Transition/Suspense subtree leaks.
I came across this from (as a Member) nuxt/nuxt#34859 - it surfaces there because  renders exactly this structure internally. I reduced it to a Vue-only repro (no Nuxt, no vue-router), which is why I'm filing it here. Conditions (all required to reproduce):

Conditional parent is a <template v-if> Fragment - switching to <div v-if> makes it disappear
<Transition mode="out-in"> - removing mode makes it disappear
A <Suspense> inside the Transition
A descendant component with async setup (so Suspense actually suspends)

What I observed while debugging: the component lifecycle looks clean - onUnmounted fires for every leaving instance. But the DOM subtree stays attached to the container anyway. This points at the out-in leave path interacting badly with suspensible Suspense: the  afterLeave callback that should call hostRemove(el) never runs, because the surrounding  itself is torn down before it gets a chance to fire.
What is expected?
Component should been removed from DOM.
What is actually happening?
Component is still staying with N copies.

title: defineProps runtime props inference misses Array from MaybeRef<T[]> in union type after upgrading to Vue 3.5.31
body:
Vue version
3.5.31
Link to minimal reproduction
https://github.com/wuchunxu/vite-prop-runtime-repro
Steps to reproduce
After upgrading Vue from 3.5.21 to 3.5.31, runtime props inference from defineProps<T>() changed for a complex union type.
I have a prop type like this:
export type FormItemOptions<T = any, Context = any> =
  MaybeRef<OptionItem[]>
  | Promise<OptionItem[]>
  | ((row: T, context: Context) => Awaitable<OptionItem[]>)
In built output, Vue generates runtime prop type as:
options: {
  type: [Promise, Function],
  default: () => []
}
Array is missing, so passing an array value triggers runtime warning:
[Vue warn]: Invalid prop: type check failed for prop "options". Expected Promise | Function, got Array
If I explicitly add OptionItem[] in the union (instead of relying only on MaybeRef<OptionItem[]>), the generated runtime type includes Array and warning disappears.
What is expected?
Runtime props inference should include Array branch (or at least not narrow in a way that rejects valid array values from MaybeRef<OptionItem[]>).
For this case, expected generated runtime type should include:
type: [Array, Promise, Function]
What is actually happening?
Generated runtime type is:
type: [Promise, Function]
which rejects array values at runtime.
System Info

Any additional comments?
This looks like a boundary case in SFC type-to-runtime props inference for complex union types involving MaybeRef<T[]>.
If this should be tracked in another Vue package (e.g. compiler-sfc), please let me know and I can move the issue with the same repro.

title: `:deep` within `:is` is not resolved when there is another selector
[Teleport] TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading 'subTree') during Suspense resolve — regression in 3.5.32
body:
Vue version
3.5.32
Link to minimal reproduction
https://play.vuejs.org/#
Steps to reproduce

Open the reproduction link (Vue 3.5.32)
Open browser console
See TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading 'subTree') on page load
Switch Vue version to 3.5.31 → error disappears

What is expected?
No error. The page renders correctly (works in 3.5.31).
What is actually happening?
Crash on page load:
Uncaught (in promise) TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading 'subTree') at move (runtime-dom.esm-browser.js:8744:28) at Object.moveTeleport [as move] (runtime-dom.esm-browser.js:3443:9) at move (runtime-dom.esm-browser.js:8752:12) at move (runtime-dom.esm-browser.js:8744:7) at move (runtime-dom.esm-browser.js:8758:9) at move (runtime-dom.esm-browser.js:8744:7) at Object.resolve (runtime-dom.esm-browser.js:9498:11)
System Info
...
Any additional comments?
Regression introduced by PR #14642.
Root cause: queuePendingMount() in Teleport.ts defers mount when parentSuspense.pendingBranch exists (including for disabled Teleports). During Suspense.resolve(), move(pendingBranch) runs before the deferred mount job. When moveTeleport encounters a disabled Teleport in REORDER mode, it iterates children — but children's vnode.component is null because mountChildren was never called.
PR #14642's test cases only covered element children (h('div', 'text')) inside Teleport. This bug requires component children (h(Comp)) inside a disabled Teleport, inside a Suspense-wrapped async component with a multi-root (Fragment) template.
Trigger conditions (all required):

<Suspense> wrapping an async component (with await in setup)
Multi-root template (Fragment) in the async component
<Teleport disabled> as a root sibling
Component child (not element) inside the Teleport


3.5.30: No error
3.5.31: No error
3.5.32: Crash

I'd like to submit a fix PR for this.
